newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIA WEEK AHEAD - Asian stocks seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: ASIA WEEK AHEAD - Asian stocks seen mixed.

text.p: Asian shares are expected to remain mixed in the coming week, with Bangkok's bourse on tenterhooks waiting for economic policy direction from a new finance minister while Hong Kong grapples with China's move to control red chips.
Friday's unexpected announcement of controls on Chinese companies listed overseas, such as the red chips in Hong Kong, could well take some of the steam out of the market.
But some analysts said sentiment underlying the rally that pushed the Hang Seng up 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, on Friday to an all-time high of 15,154.36 remained on solid ground.
The rest of the region appeared mixed, with Kuala Lumpur slated for further speculative activity while Jakarta and Manila shares are expected to trade steadily.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks are likely to drift in the coming week as investors wait for reassurance that currency market turmoil has stopped and for the Bank of Japan's survey of corporate sentiment.
Brokers said the Nikkei average was having trouble keeping its gains after setting a new closing high of 20.681.07 for calendar 1997 on June 16.
But there were no strong reasons to sell, and the Nikkei average was likely to continue to trade within a narrow range, they added.

"There are potential buyers such as pension funds, but they will probably opt to wait for the 'tankan' before buying," said Katsumichi Shimizu, general manager at Yamaichi Securities. "The downside should be fairly firm near 20,000, but gains will probably be capped by profit-taking."
The Nikkei 225 index closed 142.81 points, or 0.69 percent, weaker on Friday at 20,385.54. - - - -

HONG KONG - Share prices are braced to enjoy a record-breaking run during the final week of colonial rule in Hong Kong, feeding off euphoric sentiment surrounding the territory's return to Chinese rule, analysts said.
The Hang Seng Index staged its strongest rally in point terms on Friday, surging 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, to an all-time high of 15,154.36.
It gained 1,041.81 points, or 7.38 percent, last week.
"It looks like it will continue to go up, edging up to 15,500 possibly. It looks like there is momentum there into July 1," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.

Profit-taking could set in mid-week, and China's move to tighten controls on red chip companies could dampen sentiment in that sector, analysts said. But they said China's measures had been discounted and would make the market environment healthier, reducing excessive speculation on asset injections.

BANGKOK - Battered Thai stocks are expected to extend losses in the coming week with investors hugging the sidelines waiting for signs of policy changes following the appointment of a new finance minister, brokers said.
The SET Index fell 6.86 percent over the week to close at 480.25 despite gaining 3.33 percent on Friday on a technical rebound helped by the appointment of new Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya.

"Economic concerns still persist in the market while second quarter corporate earnings look poor. Investors are also watching if the new finance minister would change or adopt new monetary and financial measures," said Supavat Saicheua of Krungthai Thanakit.
Brokers said the lack of fresh, positive news would likely be a factor keeping investors away in the week ahead.

SINGAPORE - Dealers in Singapore said the market was nearing the end of its consolidation period and looked vulnerable to Disappointing May non-oil export data, down one percent year-on-year in nominal terms against expectations for a rise of about 3.5 percent in a Reuters poll, could lead to more selling.
"Institutions have been reducing their exposure to Singapore and there's little sign of any relief," a local bank dealer said citing weak economic figures and the upcoming budget.
Singapore'a Ministry of Finance said on Friday the 1997 budget would be announced on July 11.
Trade could be stifled further ahead of the budget talks.
The STI index ended 5.47 points up at 2,008.44 on Friday, against 1,990.12 on June 13.
SEOUL - Stocks are expected to slide in the week ahead as investors believe the market is still over-bought, brokers said.
"Consolidation is likely to continue for the time being," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
"The index would test 740 next week," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities. Brokers said small shares would be in demand in rotational buying despite overall depression.
The composite stock index ended at 760.40 on Saturday, down 31.57 points, or 3.99 percent from 791.97 the previous Saturday.

KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysian shares are expected to rise in the coming week with blue chips remaining tightly traded on lack of news while speculative plays on small-capitalised issues continue, analysts said.
"The market should go up a bit next week. But there's really no big incentive to do anything much apart from the speculative plays," said the head of research at a local stockbroking firm.

For the week, the Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 19.16 points, or 1.78 percent, higher from Friday a week earlier. The index ended at 1,097.54, up 0.06 of a point from Thursday's close.
JAKARTA - Jakarta stocks are likely to remain steady, with the index hovering around all-time highs due to strong economic fundamentals, brokers said.
"The market is likely to remain strong due to continued strong sentiment on some sectors such as the agribusiness and the automotive sectors," one broker said.
The Jakarta composite index touched an all-time high of 717.56 points in late February this year.
The World Bank said recently that Indonesia's economy has performed well recently, although significant risks remained.
On Friday, the Jakarta composite index closed at 712.22 points against the previous week's close of 698.62 points.
MANILA - Manila shares are seen trading in a limited range in the week ahead with selective positioning in issues that are expected to post better first-half earnings, traders said.

"We were caught by surprise with the gains the past days. The question is whether it will be sustained and we will likely get confirmation with second quarter company earnings. We may test the 2,950 resistance, but it's a major one to surpass," said Raul Zamora, PCCI Securities head of institutional sales.
On Friday, the main index ended 24.24 points lower at 2,881.73. But week-on-week, the index gained 80.12 points from the previous 2,801.61.

SYDNEY - Australian shares are expected to maintain their record levels after a wave of confidence from overseas investors in the resource and banking sectors carried local stocks to both a life-time high and a record close on Friday.
The All Ordinaries Index ended 19.3 points higher at 2,712.6 after hitting 2,714.2 in trade of over A$1 billion of shares.

"While this market continues to be strengthened by international markets and domestic thoughts that official interest rates may be lowered again, there's really no thought that the trend will take a reversal," said Jamie Spiteri, a Sydney-based dealer with Shaw Stockbroking.
WELLINGTON - The outlook for New Zealand shares was positive in the coming week, with the Reserve Bank likely to sanction lower interest rates due on Friday.
Extra spending of $950 million in Thursday's budget will help as well, brokers said.

New Zealand share market closed stronger on Friday, boosted by a strong performance in the forestry and paper sectors. The NZSE40 Capital Index added 57 points, or 2.4 percent, on the week and at 2423.60 was only about 20 points off its year-high.
DHAKA - Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) are likely to remain depressed in the week starting on Sunday as investors would be cautious about the budget, brokers said.

"The 1997/98 (July-June) budget announced by Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria last week has yet to be approved by parliament. Investors did not find anything encouraging in the proposed fiscal measures but they are hoping for some changes before it is approved on June 30," one broker said.
The DSE benchmark index shed 39.11 points at 1,118.29 in the week to Thursday.
